transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-01-08
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Liam Chen (Redwood SE); Sofia Ramos (Redwood CSM); Daniel Brooks (Horizon - Head of Partnerships); Priya Singh (Horizon - VP Sales); Marco Alvarez (Horizon - Solutions Architect)
Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/rec/ff-20270108-hrzn-00123

Summary:
Quick partner co-sell pipeline review focused on three prioritized Horizon opportunities (Acme Retail POC, Nova Logistics enterprise pilot, and Meridian Financial RFP response). Discussed alignment on credit/discounting, co-sell motion (roles + outreach), technical validation plan (mini-benchmarks + joint PoC), and procurement timeline. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics:
- Deal prioritization (Acme, Nova, Meridian)
- Credits / commission and co-sell split
- Technical benchmarks required (latency / token cost)
- Procurement and contract timing (SOW / NDA)
- Risks: competitive pressure (AWS Bedrock), timeline slippage, security questions

Action items (high level): see metadata action_items list above.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, we got Daniel, Priya, Marco from Horizon, and then Liam and Sofia and me from Redwood. Sound good?
[00:09] Daniel: Yep, all good on our side. Thanks for making time, Maya.
[00:12] Priya: Morning — afternoon, depending where you are. Good to be here.
[00:15] Maya: Cool. The agenda is pretty light — just want to run through the three pipeline deals you flagged, make sure we have alignment on who does what for outreach, any technical blockers, and then price/credits for co-sell. Does that work?
[00:26] Priya: Yeah, let's do it. Also we'd like to make sure procurement timeline is clear — Meridian is on a tighter SOW window.
[00:33] Maya: Noted. Liam do you want to kick off with the tech asks?
[00:36] Liam: Sure, quick one — for Acme Retail's POC they're mainly worried about latency at the 1k token tail. We can run a mini benchmark on Redwood hosted versus a small dedicated pool, show them token cost / p50/p95. I can have that in a day or two.
[00:50] Marco: That would be huge. Also Acme uses 8k context for some queries, so any notes about KV cache and prefix caching would help.
[00:58] Liam: Right, we'll capture prefix caching behavior; note that some of the model names in your doc were slightly off — the benchmark will use a redwood-verified 7B and a quantized 13B variant that we recommend.
[01:09] Daniel: Quick question on that — if we show the dedicated numbers and they're good, what's the expected discount / credits for Horizon as a partner?
[01:18] Maya: We typically do a co-sell credit structure; for partner-initiated deals we can offer partner credits for first 3 months or a commission split on net new contracted ARR. For Acme (POC -> pilot) we usually suggest 30% partner credit on the usage during POC plus referral commission if it converts; exact numbers can be flexible.
[01:36] Priya: 30% sounds reasonable as long as the handoff is clean. We need a one-pager that outlines the process we can share with their procurement folks.
[01:44] Sofia: We'll prepare a co-sell one-pager — Maya I'll work with you on the wording.
[01:48] Maya: Great. Now Nova Logistics — where are we on sales motion? Daniel?
[01:52] Daniel: Nova is interested but they want a direct exec intro. They want to see customer references and a short security packet. Also timing is Q2 close window.
[02:02] Maya: We can do an exec intro. Sofia, I'll need you to pull a couple of short reference case studies — maybe the Meridian note and the Acme early results once available.
[02:12] Sofia: On it. I also have to follow up about the security packet — should we send our standard SOC2 + ISO docs, or do they want anything specific?
[02:22] Marco: Nova asked specifically about audit logs and KMS integration. They run in GCP with a VPC peering requirement, so any notes about Redwood Private or dedicated with VPC options would be good.
[02:34] Liam: We have a standard VPC deployment path and a Private offering. For most partners we propose dedicated pools in a customer region with KMS integration — we can show a simplified network diagram.
[02:44] Priya: Perfect. How about Meridian Financial? You mentioned an RFP — status?
[02:49] Daniel: Meridian went into an RFP; they're evaluating three vendors, timeline is pretty tight — decision by end of January. They asked about on-prem options and also compliance around data residency.
[02:59] Maya: Okay that's where we might need legal and solutions to move fast. Liam, can you prepare a short SOW template + security summary? Also we might need a letter of intent if procurement wants it.
[03:11] Liam: Yes I can draft SOW skeleton, and include KMS/HSM notes; may need help from our compliance team for residency details though.
[03:18] Marco: One small note — some of the terms in the RFP use unusual acronyms, our team wasn't 100% sure on 'KV cache eviction policy' vs what Redwood calls 'prefix caching'.
[03:29] Liam: Totally, we can add a short glossary in the SOW draft.
[03:33] Daniel: Great. On procurement timeline — Asha (our procurement) will need a pricing estimate to compare. Do you have an exception process for credits if we commit to ARR?
[03:45] Maya: For committed ARR via Dedicated we can structure reserved capacity discounts and partner incentive credits. The co-sell commission would sit on top — we can model a few scenarios in the deck.
[03:55] Priya: When you say reserved capacity, is that the Redwood Dedicated offering? Any minimums?
[04:02] Maya: Yes. There are tiered minimums but for these pilots we try to avoid big minimums — often a small reserved pool + burst to hosted for scale. We'll outline options: hosted + credits, small Dedicated pool, and Private deployment if they need VPC/on-prem.
[04:18] Marco: For Meridian we probably need the Private story because of residency. Can you share an architecture slide?
[04:24] Liam: I have a simple diagram; I'll adapt it for Meridian's region and include KMS/HSM notes.
[04:30] Priya: Competition question — they flagged AWS Bedrock and Anthropic. Any quick differentiator bullets we can use?
[04:37] Maya: Sure — short version: transparent performance profiles, co-sell playbook, and a focus on production economics (batching, caching, quantization tradeoffs). We should avoid negative language but highlight predictable latency and rollout controls.
[04:51] Daniel: Sounds good. For next steps, can we get a single combined spreadsheet of the open deals with stage, expected ARR, close date, and our required Redwood deliverable?
[05:02] Sofia: I'll create the tracker and share with everyone after the call.
[05:06] Maya: Perfect. Any blockers or anything we didn't cover?
[05:09] Marco: No blockers apart from procurement timing; if we can get the SOW + security packet quickly that will help.
[05:16] Priya: Also please include an example contract clause for data residency — we saw a few weird ones.
[05:22] Liam: Will do. I'll loop in compliance.
[05:25] Daniel: One last thing — joint marketing? If Acme converts can we do a co-marketing win story?
[05:31] Maya: Definitely, we can plan a short case study and a joint webinar. We'll outline it in the co-sell deck.
[05:36] Priya: Great.
[05:37] Maya: Ok I'll summarize: Maya to send updated co-sell deck + commission scenarios; Liam to run benchmarks and draft SOW + architecture slide; Sofia to create pipeline tracker and pull references; Daniel to intro procurement. We'll try to reconvene next week if needed and aim for exec intro week of 2027-01-18.
[05:55] Daniel: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[05:57] Priya: Thanks all.
[06:00] Maya: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
